glosses: to hold, to keep in place
to hold, to reserve, to keep back
trzymając, nie pozwalać na poruszanie się czegoś lub kogoś
utrzymywać w miejscu; trzymając, nie pozwalać na zmianę pozycji
brać do rąk na krótki czas w celu przypilnowania
zajmować coś dla kogoś przez pewien czas
To act with reserve; to contain one's full measure or power.

examples.text: Don't hold back. Hit it as hard as you can.
The TSSA union, which along with the RMT represents many of the staff affected by the closures, hasn't held back on its criticism.
The dam can't hold back that much water.
Fabregas coolly slotted home after Ben Parker held back Theo Walcott and only a super Kasper Schmeichel save stopped Denilson winning it for the Gunners.

glosses: To delay the progress of, especially in school.

examples.text: He's a year older than his classmates, because he was held back in second grade.

glosses: łapać się czegoś, aby nie upaść

examples.text: Hold on tightly to the railing.

glosses: To keep; to store something for someone.

examples.text: Hold on to my umbrella while I ride the roller coaster.
I'm holding on to my trump cards until I really need them.
Hold on while I get my coat.
The departure was not unduly prolonged. In the road Mr. Love and the driver favoured the company with a brief chanty running. “Got it?—No, I ain't, 'old on,—Got it? Got it?—No, 'old on sir.”
He didn't give up his fandom when others did; he held on.
This trade held on for many years.

That scare aside, Wolves had little trouble in holding on for their first league away win of the season and their first over the Reds since little-known striker Steve Mardenborough gave them a victory at Anfield in January 1984.
